items.note: S1.1 states the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection network on triples sending (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a) and restoring scratch, and its method follows the eight-row schedule and the three stages (lines 741-763). S1.1.1 says only that central and side coefficients cancel on neighbouring triples. It omits the two neighbour rules, the fact that non-neighbours already have central coefficient zero and the self coefficient is one (752-758), and the net map (JV+RG)x.

S2.1.4 invokes 'the common-frame identity' and A speaks of frames chosen so that edges are cheap. No step says that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, or that the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1} (lines 806-817).

Nondegenerate nested labels in F^{otimes3}, the central 3->4 loss of h, L=Ich, Wm-2N+2L and both ratios are all stated correctly, and the method matches the paper (form, stage transitions, the gate decomposition). The telescoping argument that yields Wm-2N+2L is missing: source dimensions sum to N, sink dimensions to Wm-N, and gate contributions cancel (lines 891-894, 1066-1071). The edge-residual table is not given either.

It states the projections, the -P_{U_a} sources, the endpoint identity I_m and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b<W_bm. Its route matches the proof: the rank of nested projections is the dimension change, the negative source adds one rank per pair, and the endpoint difference on X_a is I_m (lines 1156-1171).

It states the phase frames, one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c<W_cm and C^{otimes m} on every role. Its sub-steps follow the proof: weight additivity mod 4, Hadamard conjugation to translation kernels, and Z signs with i^{27k} on the X_a->Y_a route.

L<N/2 giving s<Wm, the ratios 100/539 and 101/539, deficits above 20*2^-50 and tau=sigma=1-2^-50 are all present. The exact eta values and the step log m<20 with m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50) (lines 1332-1338), which turns the deficit into s/W<m^tau, are missing.

Elementary streams and controlled shifts appear only in relies-on lists and in passing ('controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time'). The lemmas' content (digit moves, split and merge, cyclic row split into W streams, the b^{O(1)} offset condition) is never stated.

It states E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones, and a shear costing exactly a interchanges plus O(V). The route matches the proof: triangular factors by descending-order controlled updates, and each one of Pi by add, interchange, subtract (lines 1425-1443). The elimination proof of the factorization and the choice of prime q are only cited.

It gives the cyclic row split into W role streams, shear frames, edges by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row, the three-update interchange, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) giving O(e^tau), and the fixed-tape parking schedule with O(V) per node. This is the paper's route.

It states O(Vu^tau) with tau=1-2^-50. The steps follow the proof: top rho digits as a row field of range q^{2rho}>=W^k padded below 2R, base-m pieces summing geometrically, and padding [2^u] to [q^e]. The unequal-width remark (1740-1762) is not covered, but it lies outside the lemma.

It covers conjugation by P_M placing kernels on slots, one child per residual vector, inverse children via (-i)^f Z C Z, row additions on whole slots, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D. All match lines 1849-1931.

The XORs at rho+iK with z restored, O(V(L^tau+1)) under the family growth, delta_bad, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B and the repair by radix sort all match the paper. The method never says that each rotation first swaps its target behind its controls with chunk-swap (lines 2117-2131), which is where the L^tau term comes from. It also describes all eight lines as guarded by parities of z.

The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) and the final O(d^{lambda'}) condition are stated. The leaf cutoff e<d^beta with F(e)=O(e) and beta=1/2 are omitted, and lambda, sigma, beta appear in S3.1.10 without being defined. The unrolling steps are absent: K<=e^{c/beta} gives overhead O(e^lambda), and the leaves give O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) (lines 2413-2430).

The layer statement (O(Vd^{lambda'}), error <sqrt2 2^-p) and the proof's structure (C recursion, guarded exact format, H_0 identity, one truncation) match. The guard bound C_0d^{C_1} is only asserted. Its derivation through the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E (lines 2511-2534) is absent.

LBF^-, F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, the error and the cost are stated correctly, and the DIF, bit reversal, grouping, layout and truncation steps follow the paper. Character cancellation F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I (omega_t=y^{2r/t}) and the argument that the reversed recursion equals F^+B^{-1} (H_0^2=I/2, lines 2869-2881) are not given.
It gives the evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the 4pr-bit bound, |h_j|<B_0/2 so centered residues recover h_j, four products with the established multiplier, and O(rp log(rp)), all as in the proof.
The error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^-p, the cost, the retained LB order and the normalization identities match lines 3414-3474. S4.3 leaves out the 1/r in the pointwise products P(u,v)=uv/r.

The identities P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA and RF_s=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A, the errors and the costs are correct, and the Neumann-series left inverse and the linewise tensor route follow the paper. The separation hypothesis theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4 is reduced to 'enough separation', and P_s, P_t are not defined.

Both identities are stated, and the proof steps (coefficient comparison, RF^+R=F^+ from t_i a unit mod s_i, the normalized convolution rule) match. The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never defined, so the first identity lacks its key quantity.

It gives b, p, d, K, T, the exponents, the sizes, the prime intervals, T/2<S<T, n^{o(1)} search and no wraparound, as in the paper. It omits alpha, gamma=2d alpha^2, eta=1/(4d), delta=1/16, and the check alpha^4 theta_i>p, so the interval in S8.3 uses an undefined eta.

It covers the isomorphism from the order of the image of x, the triangular formula, prefix-controlled shifts that preserve the valid set, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) cost with chunk-swap axis reversal, all as in the paper.

It states the twist x_d->zeta y and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+f, iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T, checks the wrap zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and notes that iota moves no payload. The twist error bound appears only later in the precision accounting.
The source-transform composition, its exact counterpart RF_s, the conjugate procedure and the six-step algorithm with its two S scalings all match the paper.

It gives E_ring, the chirp error 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, the product error, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 and the carries. The opposite-transform step (3E_s+2), E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28*2^gamma T^2L and the use of gamma<=b/4 (lines 4692-4726) are skipped.

It states the final O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), min g_i=2^-181=2kappa, the setup and sorting o(V) and the schoolbook cutoff. The seven normalized costs and their powers are not tabulated, and nothing says that the minimal margin is g_2=eps c(1-tau), from chunk exchanges (lines 4822-4852).
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n conjecture in this model. It does not explain why, namely that the eventual lower bound requires T_A(n)>=c_A n lg n and the bound gives a liminf of zero.

errors.says: Eight packed cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, each controlled by x and guarded by parities of z, flip the selected parities.
errors.paper: The eight lines alternately update y testing the parity of z and update z testing the parity of y (eq. eight-packed-additions; 'for a line updating z, interchange y and z'). Each rotation first moves its target behind its two controls by a chunk swap of cost O(VL^tau), and the L^tau term comes from these swaps.

errors.says: Scaling the opposite transform of the stored pointwise products (F^-f)(F^-g) by M gives exactly M_r(f,g).
errors.paper: The pointwise products are normalized, P(u,v)=uv/r, and M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM). Without the 1/r the scaling yields (f*g)/M.

errors.says: The central coefficient and the side coefficient cancel for all neighbouring distinct triples.
errors.paper: Correct for neighbours. The full net map also uses that non-neighbouring distinct triples already have central coefficient zero (intersection 0 or 2 in the bit case, 1 in the complex case) and that the self coefficient is one. The step omits this, so it does not by itself establish y<-y+x.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route: scalar bank exchange, nested labels with L<N/2, projection and phase interfaces with s<Wm, matrix shear, the power-width recurrence and the chunk swap, then the phase-frame layer recursion, synthetic transforms, resampling, CRT, twist, precision and cost totals. It thins where the common-frame identity is only named, where the layer recurrence's unrolling (leaf cutoff, K<=e^{c/beta}) and the guard-depth recurrence are asserted rather than derived, and where the cost table behind min g_i=2kappa is not reproduced.

steps.note: It covers triples of a 100-element set, banks X_a,Y_a, the three-stage linear exchange to (-Y_a,X_a) (a swap over F_2), and restoration of every scratch wire. N=binom(h,3)^3 is never written out; m appears only as the dimension of F^{otimes3}.
Frames are named and used ('common-frame identity', Phi_M composing additively). No step says that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, or that the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}.
It has nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional F^{otimes3}, nested labels on every edge, and central 3->4 edges as the only decreasing edges, each losing h.
It has rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, and the negative source projection adding one rank per data pair.
It gives the sum of absolute changes Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.
It has L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, hence s<Wm. The deficit N-2L is implicit in s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b<W_bm.
It has M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m on every role, giving H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
It has the E_1 Pi E_2 factorization, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) per rank-a shear, and edge ranks summing to s recursive calls.

It has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), deficits above 20*2^-50 giving s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50, and F_k=O(e^tau). The supporting step log m<20 (m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)) is left implicit.

central.summary: P03 reconstructs the central saving almost completely: the fixed exchange network, nested labels with the central-wire loss, rank equal to dimension change plus N source ranks, the budget Wm-N+2L, L/N<1/2, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. The one real gap is the frame mechanism (C2): the common-frame identity is invoked by name but its content (frames commute with pointwise gates, so the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}) is never stated.
